Colons Check

Source: R/colons_check.R
colons_check.Rd

Verify that all the functions used inside a function are preceded by a package attribution. For instance: base::mean() and not mean(), or saferDev:::.base_op_check() and not .base_op_check(). Warning: does not check that the package is the good one. Use all_args_here() for that.

Usage

colons_check(
  x,
  export = FALSE,
  out_path = ".",
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

x

a function name, written without quotes and brackets.

export

Single logical value. Export the modified code into a .R file? If TRUE, the modified function is not returned but only exported. The name of the file is the name of the tested function, with _safer added at the end (e.g., test_safer.R). The written code is the code of the submitted function, with its comments and indentation, only modified by the added package attributions (see the Details section). An error is returned if the file already exists in out_path, and if the tested function is not designated by a function name (like test or package::test), i.e., written by an inline definition (like function(x){x}) or by a component writing (like FUN_LIST$fun). If FALSE (default), the modified function is not written but returned.

out_path

Single character string indicating the pathway of the folder where to export the modified code. out_path = "." (default) means the R working directory set by the user. A non-existing directory, NULL or an empty string ("") returns an error. Ignored if export is FALSE.

safer_check

Single logical value. Perform some "safer" checks? If TRUE, checkings are performed before main code running (see the safer-r project): 1) correct lib_path argument value 2) required functions and related packages effectively present in local R libraries and 3) R classical operators (like "<-") not overwritten by another package because of the R scope. Must be set to FALSE if this function is used inside another "safer" function to avoid pointless multiple checkings.

lib_path

Vector of characters specifying the absolute pathways of the directories containing the required packages for the function, if not in the default directories. Useful when R packages are not installed in the default directories because of lack of admin rights. More precisely, lib_path is passed through the new argument of .libPaths() so that the new library paths are unique(c(new, .Library.site, .Library)). Warning: .libPaths() is restored to the initial paths, after function execution. Ignored if NULL (default) or if the safer_check argument is FALSE: only the pathways specified by the current .libPaths() are used for package calling.

error_text

Single character string used to add information in error messages returned by the function, notably if the function is inside other functions, which is practical for debugging. Example: error_text = " INSIDE <PACKAGE_1>::<FUNCTION_1> INSIDE <PACKAGE_2>::<FUNCTION_2>.". If NULL, converted into "".

Value

A table-like text message indicating the missing :: or ::: or a message saying that everything seems fine.

The message is always printed (see the Details section).

In addition, if the export argument is FALSE (default), the function returns NULL if no basic function required a package attribution, or the modified function if basic functions were modified (see the Details section).

If the export argument is TRUE, the modified code is exported in the .R file specified by the out_path argument, instead of being returned, and a message indicating where the modified code has been exported is printed.

Table-like: column 1, the line number in the function code (starting at the "<- function" line, i.e., without counting the #' header lines); column 2, the function name; column 3, the code preceding the function name.

With missing :: or :::, the message also indicates if internal functions are created inside the checked function code, since these functions cannot have :: or :::.

Details

The result is used to modify the code inside the tested function like this: <PACKAGE>::<FUNCTION> (or <PACKAGE>:::<FUNCTION> for function names starting by a dot).

Since saferDev v3.0.0, the modified function is returned: the package attributions of the basic R functions, as indicated in the "INSIDE test(), SOME :: OR ::: ARE MISSING BEFORE BASIC FUNCTIONS" section of the returned message, are added to the submitted function code, and the modified function is returned using return(). The package attributions of the other functions, as indicated in the "INSIDE test(), SOME :: OR ::: ARE MISSING BEFORE OTHER FUNCTIONS" section of the returned message, are NOT added automatically, because the correct package cannot be determined reliably: a base::warning() is issued instead (in addition to the printed message). NULL is returned if no basic function required a package attribution.

The modification is only performed on the code lines indicated in the "INSIDE test(), SOME :: OR ::: ARE MISSING BEFORE BASIC FUNCTIONS" section of the message, which is the same analysis as the one performed by colons_check() itself: functions written between quotes or preceded by $ are not modified, and internal functions (created inside the tested function) are not modified either. The analysis is performed on the code with comments removed and multiple spaces collapsed, but the package attributions are added to the code of the submitted function as printed: the returned (and exported) function therefore keeps the comments and the indentation of the submitted function. Warning: comments are only present when the submitted function carries its source references (attribute srcref, e.g., a function defined in the console or in a file loaded with keep.source = TRUE). Otherwise, as for compiled package functions, the code printed by R (without comments and reindented) is used. The modified function is returned with the environment of the submitted function, so that the functions used inside it still resolve the same way. If the modified code does not parse (a rare situation, e.g., a function name split across lines in a way the analyzer could not handle correctly), this is an internal bug: an internal error is returned when export = TRUE, and the submitted function is returned unchanged, with no error, when export = FALSE.

The name of the exported file (when export = TRUE) is the name of the submitted function, as written by the user, with _safer added at the end, e.g., test_safer.R for colons_check(x = test). If the submitted function was written as package::function, like colons_check(x = saferDev::test), the name is test_safer.R (the package name is not part of the file name). The exported file contains an assignment of the modified function: test_safer <- function(...) ..., so that base::source()ing it recreates the modified function. Warning: the tested function must be designated by a function name (like test or package::test) when export = TRUE: an inline definition (like function(x){x}) or a component writing (like FUN_LIST$fun) returns an error, because the name of the exported file could not be determined reliably.

Pre-check: the submitted function is first checked by lambda_check(): if some lambda functions are written with the \(x) shorthand, an error is returned asking to run saferDev::lambda_check() first, because the \ writings are not managed by the text-based detection of colons_check(). As in lambda_check(), the \(x) writing is only detectable in a function carrying its source references (attribute srcref): a compiled or loaded package function prints function(x), so that the pre-check silently passes in that case.

More precisely, colons_check() verifies that all the strings before an opening bracket ( are preceded by ::.

::: are not checked per se, because incorrect writing, like saferDev::.colons_check_message() returns an error when executing the tested function, and because base:::sum() is as ok as base::sum(). In the same manner, more than three colons are not checked because it returns an error when executing the tested function.

Warning: colons_check() cannot check function names written without brackets, like in the FUN argument of some functions, e.g., sapply(1:3, FUN = as.character).

The Perl regex used to detect a function name is: "([a-zA-Z]|\.[a-zA-Z._])[a-zA-Z0-9._]*\s*\(".

Currently, colons_check() cannot detect functions written between quotes, like "+"() or "rownames<-"(x, "a").

Function names preceded by $ are not considered.

The following R functions are skipped: "function", "if", "for", "while", "repeat" and "else".

Most of the time, colons_check() does not check inside comments, but some unexpected writing could dupe colons_check(). Please, report here if it is the case.

The returned line numbers are indicative, depending on which source is checked. For instance, saferDev::report (compiled) has not the same line numbers as its source file (source file). Notably, compiled functions do not have comments anymore, compared to the same source function sourced into the working environment. In addition, the counting starts at the "<- function" line, i.e., without counting the #' header lines potentially present in source files.

Of note, during package creation, the devtools::check() command tells which functions where wrongly attributed to package. Example:


checking dependencies in R code ... WARNING
  '::' or ':::' import not declared from: 'sbase'
  Missing or unexported objects:
    'base::dev.off' 'base::graphics.off' 'base::hcl' 'base::par' 'base::read.table' 'saferGG::report'

Examples

# Warning: these examples may not work well when using the "Run examples" link 
# because of a particular environment. Please, copy-paste in a local environment.
# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/colons_check.html
fun1 <- function(x){
    y <- mean(x) # mean() written without base::
    base::return(y)
}
fun1_safer <- saferDev::colons_check(fun1) # base:: added before mean()
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun1(), SOME :: OR ::: ARE MISSING BEFORE BASIC FUNCTIONS:
#> 
#> LINE	FUN		STRING_BEFORE
#> 3	mean		y <- 
#> 
fun1_safer # corrected function
#> function (x) 
#> {
#>     y <- base::mean(x)
#>     base::return(y)
#> }
#> <environment: 0x56555c8584f8>
# Write the corrected function in the fun1_safer.R file of a new temporary folder:
tempo_dir <- base::tempfile(pattern = "dir", tmpdir = base::tempdir(), fileext = "")
base::dir.create(path = tempo_dir, showWarnings = TRUE, recursive = FALSE, mode = "0777")
saferDev::colons_check(x = fun1, export = TRUE, out_path = tempo_dir)
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun1(), SOME :: OR ::: ARE MISSING BEFORE BASIC FUNCTIONS:
#> 
#> LINE	FUN		STRING_BEFORE
#> 3	mean		y <- 
#> 
#> MODIFIED CODE EXPORTED IN:
#> /tmp/RtmpCGuf8f/dir1732592cec6a/fun1_safer.R
#>
